title: Deploying Services: Replicas, Scaling & Rolling Updates ⚡
description: Create, scale, and update services seamlessly across a cluster of Docker nodes.

slides.title: Creating a Service 🛠️
slides.content:
# `docker service create`

Similar to `docker run` but for a cluster.

```bash
docker service create --name web --replicas 3 -p 80:80 nginx:alpine
```

- `--replicas`: number of container instances.
- `-p`: publishes the port across the swarm (routing mesh).
- Swarm schedules the containers across available nodes.

Check services:
```bash
docker service ls
docker service ps web   # see tasks (containers) for this service
```

slides.title: The Routing Mesh 🌐
slides.content:
# Port Publishing in Swarm

When you publish a service port, **every node** in the swarm listens on that port, even if it’s not running a replica. Traffic is automatically load‑balanced to a container running the service.

- This is called **routing mesh**.
- Works with ingress overlay network.
- You can hit any node on the published port and get the service.

> This means you don’t need an external load balancer for basic distribution.

quizData.question: In Swarm, if you publish a service on port 80, how do clients access it?

options.text: Through any node's IP on port 80, and traffic is routed to a replica
Only through the node running the replica
You must configure an external load balancer

quizData.explanation: The routing mesh makes all nodes participate in serving the published port.

slides.title: Scaling Services 📈
slides.content:
# `docker service scale`

Change the number of replicas on the fly:
```bash
docker service scale web=5
```

Swarm will add or remove containers to match the desired count.

Check the distribution:
```bash
docker service ps web
```

> Zero downtime: existing replicas continue serving while new ones start.

slides.title: Scaling Demo 🧮
slides.codeSnippet:
# Start a service with 2 replicas
docker service create --name demo --replicas 2 alpine sleep 3600

# See tasks
docker service ps demo

# Scale up to 4
docker service scale demo=4

# See new tasks
docker service ps demo

slides.title: Rolling Updates 🔄
slides.content:
# Update a Service Without Downtime

```bash
docker service update --image nginx:1.25 web
```

By default, Swarm performs a **rolling update**:
- Replaces one replica at a time with the new version.
- If the update fails, it can rollback automatically (configurable with `--update-failure-action rollback`).

You can control:
- `--update-parallelism` (how many replicas to update simultaneously)
- `--update-delay` (wait between batches)

Monitor with:
```bash
docker service ps web
```

> You can also rollback manually: `docker service rollback web`.

quizData.question: What is the default update strategy for a Docker Swarm service?

options.text: Delete all replicas and recreate them
Rolling update – replace replicas one by one

quizData.explanation: Swarm performs rolling updates by default to maintain service availability.

slides.title: Inspecting & Removing Services 🔍
slides.content:
# `docker service inspect` & `docker service rm`

Get detailed info:
```bash
docker service inspect --pretty web
```

Remove a service (all its tasks are stopped):
```bash
docker service rm web
```

> `docker service logs` also works to view logs from all replicas.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Placement Constraints
Control where replicas run:
```bash
docker service create --constraint node.role==worker ...
```
Or use node labels for more fine‑grained placement.
